sentences.text: COMMON ORDER
Mr.Rabu Manohar, learned Senior Central Government Panel Counsel accepts notice for respondents 1 to 3.
Mr.A.P.Srinivas, learned Senior Standing Counsel accepts notice for respondents 4 and 5.
Heard both.
By consent, the writ petitions are taken up for final disposal.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India,
by proceedings dated 3.6.2016, issued certain directions and as a result of which, it is further submitted that no orders need be passed in these writ petitions in the light of the said directions.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. The learned counsel for the respondents submit that they do not have any instructions in the matters and that the directions appear to have been downloaded from the official website.
4. Be that as it may, the petitioner states that no orders are required in these writ petitions.
For better appreciation, the directions issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India dated 3.6.2016 are extracted hereunder :

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
"F.No.15017/131/2014-FSSAI/Legal Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (A Statutory Authority under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India) FDA Bhawan, Kotla Road, New Delhi-110002 -----------------------------------------------
The 3rd June 2016 Subject : Direction under Section 16(5) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 regarding duty free shop at all airports of India.
Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) had, in exercise of the power conferred by Clause (d) of Sub-Section (2) of Section 18 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 operationalized the Food Safety and Standards (Food Import)
Regulations, 2016.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Clause 14.3 of the notice of operationalization stipulated that 'The provisions of the Act and the Regulations will be applicable to all duty free shops at all Airports of India'.
2.

After due consideration of representations received from various stakeholders, the above mentioned issue has been re-examined and it has been decided that duty free shops would be outside the ambit of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and Regulations made thereunder.
Accordingly, Clause 14.3 of the notice referred to above stands deleted with immediate effect till such time the import regulations are finally notified.
